title: Invoice reconciliation errors
honesty_boundary: This tool is a scoping aid for checkable trial definitions, not a guarantee of outcomes. Synthetic demo claims describe fictional examples and no real engagements. Evidence pointers are supplied by the input and are not independently inspected.
problem: A small finance team manually compares invoice exports and spends time finding total mismatches.

artifact.name: Invoice reconciliation validator
artifact.format: A runnable standard-library Python script with CSV input and output.
artifact.scope_limit: The artifact is limited to the mapped capabilities and listed acceptance criteria.

mapped_claims.claim: compare invoice totals and flag mismatches

acceptance_criteria.condition: The output directory contains exactly 3 files: reconciled.csv, exceptions.csv, README.md.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: List the output directory and compare the filenames with the required set.

acceptance_criteria.condition: Given the 10-row synthetic invoice input, reconciled.csv contains 8 matching rows and exceptions.csv contains 2 mismatch rows.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Run the script on the supplied synthetic CSV, then count data rows in both output CSV files.

acceptance_criteria.condition: Each exceptions.csv row includes invoice_id, expected_total, observed_total, difference columns.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Open exceptions.csv and compare its header row with the 4 required column names.

assumptions: The buyer supplies one UTF-8 CSV with invoice_id, expected_total, and observed_total columns.
Currency values use decimal notation with a period separator.
exclusions: No connection to accounting software or live financial data.
No tax, foreign exchange, or accounting policy advice.

fixed_price.pricing_rule: GBP 750 per day plus GBP 125 per acceptance criterion; day count follows the documented scope threshold.
